dz.headline: Algeria's ruling FLN wins 90 of 407 seats as turnout hits record-low 21%
dz.body: Algeria's ruling National Liberation Front won the most seats in the country's parliamentary elections, the election board said Monday, securing 90 out of 407 in the July 2 vote. The vote saw a record-low turnout, with just 21 percent of the 25-million electorate casting ballots, and was marred by public apathy and controversy over the government's disqualification of roughly a third of would-be candidates. The National Democratic Rally and the Future Front followed as the next largest blocs in the new assembly.
dz.why: Record-low participation signals eroding public confidence in the political system even as the establishment retains full legislative control.

dz.headline: Sonatrach signs new Germany gas-supply deal, cementing Berlin energy pivot
dz.body: Algeria is strengthening its role as one of Europe's most important alternative energy suppliers after state-owned energy company Sonatrach signed a new agreement with German energy group VNG to increase pipeline natural gas deliveries to Germany from January 2027. The deal came during President Abdelmadjid Tebboune's state visit to Berlin, days after Sonatrach completed its first-ever LNG shipment to Germany on July 2. An Algerian-German economic forum on the sidelines of the visit produced more than 30 agreements covering hydrocarbons, renewable energy, pharmaceuticals and advanced technologies.
dz.why: Deeper pipeline and LNG ties with Europe's largest gas consumer lock in export revenue and diplomatic leverage for Algeria's hydrocarbon-dependent economy.

dz.headline: Bank of Algeria holds rate near 2.75% as fiscal deficit widens to 11.5% of GDP
dz.body: In August 2025 the Bank of Algeria lowered its key interest rate by 25 basis points to 2.75% and cut the reserve requirement ratio to 2% to support bank lending and non-hydrocarbon growth. Despite elevated gas revenue, Algeria's fiscal balance stood at -11.5% of GDP in 2025, the widest gap of any oil exporter in the MENA region, and is expected to widen toward -12% in 2026. The debt-to-GDP ratio rose an estimated 12% year-on-year in 2025 and is projected to reach 80% of GDP by 2030.
dz.why: A widening budget gap despite strong gas exports raises pressure for tax or subsidy reform down the line.

dz.headline: Bus crash kills at least 25 people in Algeria
dz.body: At least 25 people have been killed and dozens more injured in a bus crash in Algeria, according to Al Jazeera. The incident adds to a series of deadly road accidents that have drawn attention to transport safety standards in the country.
dz.why: Road-safety enforcement and inter-city bus regulation face renewed scrutiny after the high death toll.

dz.headline: Fire kills 11 at state-run Algiers orphanage
dz.body: Eleven people died and 19 were injured after a fire swept through a state-run child welfare home in east Algiers, published July 16, 2026. The blaze has raised questions about fire-safety standards at public care facilities.
dz.why: The death toll is likely to trigger inspections of safety conditions at other state-run institutions.

dz.headline: Algiers Stock Exchange cap jumps 43% to $5.73 billion, more listings planned
dz.body: The capitalization of the Algiers Stock Exchange reached 745.4 billion dinars (about $5.73 billion) at the end of June 2025, compared with about 520 billion dinars at the beginning of January, an increase of 43% over the first half of the year, according to Cosob data. The exchange, created in 1997, currently counts only eight listed companies: Alliance Assurances, Biopharm, El Aurassi, Saidal, CrÃƒÂ©dit Populaire d'AlgÃƒÂ©rie, AOM Invest SPA, Banque de DÃƒÂ©veloppement Local and Moustachir. The regulator expects two to three additional IPOs in 2026 as authorities push to deepen a market that still plays a marginal financing role in the economy.
dz.why: New listings could gradually widen financing options for Algerian firms beyond state bank lending.

dz.headline: USM Alger wins CAF Confederation Cup, hailed by President Tebboune
dz.body: Algerian President Abdelmadjid Tebboune congratulated USM Alger after the club won the CAF Confederation Cup title following its recent victory, according to AL24 News. The win adds to a strong run for Algerian club football on the continental stage.
dz.why: The continental title boosts national sporting pride and USM Alger's commercial and sponsorship profile.

dz.headline: Algeria's inflation seen rising to 3.5% in 2026 on fuel and wage increases
dz.body: Inflation is projected to rise to 3.5% in 2026, driven in part by an increase in retail fuel prices introduced in January 2026, although those prices remain relatively low by regional standards. A minimum-wage increase in 2026 is also likely to add upward price pressure. The Algerian dinar weakened against the U.S. dollar in 2025 and declined more sharply against the euro, reflecting weaker relative performance versus other African currencies.
dz.why: Faster inflation alongside a softer dinar could squeeze household purchasing power despite subsidised fuel prices.

ao.headline: Angola floats 15% of Unitel on BODIVA in landmark IPO
ao.body: Angola has begun selling roughly 15% of Unitel, its dominant mobile operator, on the Luanda-based BODIVA exchange, with the investor roadshow starting the week of July 6, 2026. The state took full ownership of Unitel in October 2022 after seizing stakes previously held by Isabel dos Santos and an associate as part of President JoÃƒÂ£o LourenÃƒÂ§o's anti-corruption drive. Officials have called the listing the largest yet on the Angolan Debt and Securities Exchange.
ao.why: A successful float would deepen Angola's still-thin capital market and test investor appetite for state assets beyond oil.

ao.headline: Angola's inflation cools to 10.9% in May, three-year low
ao.body: Consumer prices in Angola rose 10.9% year-on-year in May, down from an 11.6% increase in April, marking the softest reading since 2015 according to FocusEconomics. The slowdown follows a string of interest-rate cuts and a period of relative kwanza stability that has eased pressure on household budgets.
ao.why: Cooling inflation gives the central bank more room to keep easing policy without reigniting currency pressure.

ao.headline: Angola's GDP growth eases to 5.3% in first quarter
ao.body: Angola's economy expanded 5.3% year-on-year in the first quarter of 2026, slowing from 5.7% growth in the prior quarter, according to FocusEconomics. Growth was supported by easing weakness in the oil sector alongside stronger non-oil activity in transport, digital services and manufacturing.
ao.why: Steady, above-trend growth signals Angola's diversification push is gaining traction even as a favorable base effect fades.

ao.headline: Angola's cholera cases fall 23% in May to 1,742
ao.body: Angola reported 1,742 new cholera cases and 34 deaths in May 2026, a 23% drop in cases and 13% fall in deaths from April, according to a World Health Organization update. Benguela, Luanda and Icolo e Bengo provinces accounted for the bulk of the roughly 4,852 cases and 96 deaths logged nationwide between January and May 2026.
ao.why: The decline suggests outbreak-response measures are working, but Angola remains among Africa's hardest-hit countries this year.

ao.headline: US adds Isabel dos Santos to anti-kleptocracy visa blacklist
ao.body: The United States on June 2, 2026 designated Isabel dos Santos, daughter of Angola's late former president JosÃƒÂ© Eduardo dos Santos, under its Anti-Kleptocracy and Human Rights Visa Restrictions program. Courts in Angola, Portugal, the UK and the US have already frozen billions of dollars in assets tied to dos Santos, who has never been convicted of a crime and denies wrongdoing.
ao.why: The move keeps international pressure on Angola's most prominent corruption case, with implications for asset-recovery efforts tied to state firms Sonangol and Unitel.

ao.headline: Lobito Corridor railway closes $753 million financing deal
ao.body: The Lobito Atlantic Railway consortium achieved financial close on a $753 million financing package in July 2026 to upgrade the 1,300-km rail line linking Angola's Lobito port to the DRC border, according to Engineering News. The investment covers 1,555 wagons and 35 locomotives and is expected to lift the corridor's freight capacity roughly tenfold, to about 4.6 million tonnes a year, while cutting mineral-transport costs by an estimated 30%.
ao.why: More capacity on the corridor strengthens Angola's bid to become the main Atlantic gateway for Congolese copper and cobalt exports.

ao.headline: Angola's opposition UNITA hires US lobbyist ahead of 2027 vote
ao.body: UNITA, Angola's main opposition party, has retained veteran US conservative lobbyist Duncan Sellars as it seeks to challenge the ruling MPLA's decades-long hold on power ahead of the 2027 general election, according to The Africa Report.
ao.why: Outside lobbying support signals UNITA is trying to internationalize its campaign as it prepares for its next test at the ballot box.

ao.headline: Agriculture overtakes oil's share of Angola's GDP, official says
ao.body: Agriculture now accounts for roughly a quarter of Angola's GDP compared with oil's 15%, according to economic czar JosÃƒÂ© de Lima Massano, cited by The Africa Report as marking a structural shift for the petro-state. Oil-rich Angola still imports 70% of its refined petroleum, and is following Nigeria's lead in trying to end its fuel-import dependency.
ao.why: If sustained, the shift would mark a milestone in Angola's long-stated goal of reducing dependence on volatile oil revenue.

bj.headline: Romuald Wadagni sworn in as Benin's president, succeeding Patrice Talon
bj.body: Romuald Wadagni, Benin's long-serving finance minister, took office as the country's ninth president on May 24, 2026, succeeding Patrice Talon. Wadagni, the ruling coalition's chosen candidate, moved quickly to form a new government after a landslide election win, according to reporting compiled by allAfrica.
bj.why: A smooth handover after a decade of Talon-era economic policy signals continuity for investors and donors watching West Africa's coup-hit region.

bj.headline: South African court delays Kemi Seba extradition case to Benin until Aug. 11
bj.body: A Pretoria court has postponed proceedings in the extradition case of pan-African activist Kemi Seba to August 11, 2026, leaving him in pretrial custody. Benin is seeking his return over allegations of incitement to rebellion tied to the failed December 2025 coup attempt against President Talon.
bj.why: The ruling will test how neighboring judiciaries handle politically charged coup-related cases and could reshape ties between Cotonou and Pretoria.

bj.headline: Benin jails about 30 people, mostly soldiers, over foiled December coup
bj.body: Beninese authorities jailed roughly 30 people, most of them soldiers, on charges linked to the failed December 7, 2025 attempt to oust President Talon, according to legal sources cited by AFP. The alleged ringleader, Lieutenant Colonel Pascal Tigri, and other mutineers remain at large.
bj.why: Ongoing prosecutions and a manhunt for the coup leader keep security risk elevated for businesses and travelers in Cotonou.

bj.headline: Ruling coalition sweeps all 109 seats in Benin's January legislative vote
bj.body: Two parties backing President Talon won every one of the 109 seats in parliament in the January 11, 2026 legislative elections, after the opposition failed to clear the 10% national vote threshold required to sit, according to the World Bank. The vote preceded the April 12 presidential election that brought Wadagni to power.
bj.why: A one-party legislature removes a check on the new president's agenda heading into 2026 policy decisions.

bj.headline: Benin's economy set to grow 6.4-6.8% through 2026 on port, industrial-zone buildout
bj.body: The African Development Bank projects Benin's growth rate at 6.4% in 2025, rising to 6.8% in 2026, driven by construction and manufacturing tied to port and road works. Growth in 2024 already reached 7.5%, up from 6.4% in 2023, with the Glo-DjigbÃƒÂ© Industrial Zone a key driver, while inflation is expected to stay below 2% through 2026.
bj.why: Sustained high growth and low inflation support the case for continued foreign investment in Benin's industrial push.

bj.headline: Benin's cotton sector posts a record season as CFA-zone producers diverge
bj.body: Benin recorded a record cotton season even as Mali's output weakened sharply and Burkina Faso moved to nationalize its sector, according to The Africa Report. The divergence reflects differing political choices across CFA franc-zone producers amid a global price war in the commodity.
bj.why: A record harvest bolsters export earnings and rural incomes in Benin's largest cash-crop sector.

bj.headline: BIIC bank profit jumps 48% in first quarter as BRVM shares climb
bj.body: Shares of Banque Internationale pour l'Industrie et le Commerce du BÃƒÂ©nin (BICB), listed on the regional BRVM exchange, closed at 7,690 CFA francs, roughly flat on the session, after the bank reported a 48% jump in first-quarter 2026 profit, according to Sikafinance. Benin's Loterie Nationale (LNBB) shares closed the same session down 3.51% at 4,400 CFA francs.
bj.why: Strong bank earnings underline growing investor interest in Benin's expanding footprint on the regional stock market.

bj.headline: Underwater drones find thriving coral reef off Benin's coast presumed dead for decades
bj.body: Researchers using underwater drones discovered a coral reef off Benin's coast that had been presumed dead for more than 60 years, finding it teeming with marine life, according to reporting aggregated by NewsNow. The find adds a rare positive data point for West Africa's marine ecosystems amid regional coastal erosion concerns.
bj.why: The discovery could boost marine conservation funding and eco-tourism interest along Benin's Atlantic coastline.

bw.headline: Anglo American picks Gareth Penny-led group as preferred buyer for 85% De Beers stake
bw.body: <cite index="40-1,40-2,40-3">Anglo American picked a group led by one of its former executives as its preferred bidder for an 85% stake in De Beers, with the Global Diamond Consortium led by Gareth Penny selected from three shortlisted groups following a bidding process, according to Botswana's defense minister Moeti Mohwasa.</cite> <cite index="40-4">Botswana holds the remaining 15% of the world's largest diamond miner alongside pre-emptive rights, giving Gaborone full power to match the offer, buy the stake independently, or join forces with a third party.</cite> <cite index="43-1">Botswana's government has indicated the transaction is expected to close by the fourth quarter of 2026.</cite>
bw.why: The outcome will decide how much control Botswana gains over the diamond trade that drives most of its export earnings and government revenue.

bw.headline: Botswana widens foot-and-mouth infected zones as beef exports come under threat
bw.body: <cite index="24-2,24-3">Botswana's foot-and-mouth disease crisis is escalating, with government expanding infected zones and tightening restrictions, after an Extraordinary Government Gazette dated April 4, 2026 declared a vast stretch of southern Botswana an official infected area.</cite> <cite index="24-11">Movement of all cloven-hoofed animals, including cattle, goats and sheep, is strictly prohibited within, into or out of affected zones, and authorities are empowered to seize or destroy livestock deemed a disease risk.</cite> <cite index="24-7">The agriculture sector fears the outbreak could cripple Botswana's beef industry, a key export earner already under pressure from recurring disease outbreaks.</cite>
bw.why: Continued outbreaks risk shutting export-quality beef zones out of premium markets like the EU, hitting rural incomes and foreign-currency earnings.

bw.headline: Growth forecasts diverge as Botswana unemployment holds near 27.6%
bw.body: <cite index="50-9">The African Development Bank projects Botswana's real GDP growth at 1.2% in 2026 and 3.5% in 2027, supported by renewed mining investment and nonmining services activity.</cite> <cite index="50-6">Unemployment stands at 27.6% overall and 38.2% for youth, alongside high inequality.</cite> <cite index="56-1,56-5">A separate World Bank report projects growth of about 3.2% in 2026 on a diamond-production recovery, but cautions that momentum in the non-mining economy is likely to remain subdued.</cite>
bw.why: Slow, diamond-dependent growth alongside high youth joblessness keeps pressure on government to speed up job creation and diversification plans.

bw.headline: Botswana Stock Exchange turnover surges as trading volumes hit records
bw.body: <cite index="16-3">The Botswana Stock Exchange hit records in terms of the value of shares bought and sold in the first six months of the year, with turnover rising nearly six times compared with the same period last year, despite the broader slowdown in the economy.</cite> <cite index="10-11">The benchmark BSE Domestic Companies Index closed at 11,188.19, representing a 1-week gain of 0.27% and a year-to-date gain of 1.43%.</cite>
bw.why: Rising liquidity on the local bourse signals renewed investor interest even as the broader economy struggles with weak diamond output.

bw.headline: President Boko touts hemp trials as diversification push away from diamonds
bw.body: According to a government notice, <cite index="21-1">President Boko hailed successful hemp trials as a key step in economic rebuild.</cite> The announcement forms part of a wider push by the administration to broaden Botswana's revenue base beyond diamond mining.
bw.why: Any commercially viable alternative crop could offer rural jobs and export income as diamond revenues remain volatile.

bw.headline: RDC Properties cleared to pursue stake bid in rival PrimeTime
bw.body: <cite index="16-4">An investigative committee of the Botswana Stock Exchange has given RDC Properties the green light to proceed with its long-suspended bid for a stake in property sector rival PrimeTime.</cite> The clearance ends a period of regulatory uncertainty over the transaction between the two listed property firms.
bw.why: A consolidation between two BSE-listed property companies could reshape competition in Botswana's commercial real estate sector.

bw.headline: Palapye council leadership dispute heads to Gaborone High Court
bw.body: <cite index="3-1">A legal battle has erupted over the leadership of the Palapye District Council, with Botswana Patriotic Front councillor David Ikanyeng approaching the Gaborone High Court on an urgent basis to challenge a directive issued by the Minister of Local Government and Traditional Affairs, Ketlhalefile Motshegwa.</cite> <cite index="3-2">The urgent application is before Justice Itumeleng Segopolo.</cite>
bw.why: The outcome could set a precedent for how much authority central government ministers hold over local council leadership disputes.

bw.headline: Opposition BCP president challenges party to decide on taking power
bw.body: <cite index="5-3">Botswana Congress Party president Dumelang Saleshando has challenged party members to make a defining political choice on whether they are prepared to take over government or remain just an opposition party.</cite> The remarks come as opposition parties reposition themselves following the ruling coalition's rise to power.
bw.why: Internal debate within opposition ranks could shape how competitive Botswana's next election cycle becomes.

bf.headline: TraorÃƒÂ©'s junta faces mounting rights scrutiny as CIVICUS adds Burkina Faso to watchlist
bf.body: Captain Ibrahim TraorÃƒÂ©, who seized power in a 2022 coup, has become one of Africa's most recognisable military leaders even as restrictions on political activity intensify, according to Al Jazeera. CIVICUS added the country to its July 2026 Watchlist over what it called a deterioration in civic freedoms, including curbs on civil society groups, journalists and dissenting voices, while Amnesty International has criticized the dissolution of several NGOs and the UN human rights office in the country has closed.
bf.why: Continued closure of civic space signals further isolation for foreign NGOs, media and diplomats operating in the country.

bf.headline: State miner SOPAMIB wins permit for Bouboulou gold project as nationalisation push widens
bf.body: Burkina Faso has awarded an industrial mining permit to state-owned miner SOPAMIB for the Bouboulou gold project, advancing the government's push for greater state control of the mining sector, according to Reuters. The project in the north-central Yako commune will require more than 32 billion CFA francs ($56.1 million) in investment and is expected to run for over 15 years; the mines minister called it a break from a model that left development largely to private operators.
bf.why: Expanding state ownership of mines could reshape revenue flows and raise risk premiums for remaining foreign gold operators.

bf.headline: 4.5 million people need urgent aid in Burkina Faso as conflict and climate shocks bite
bf.body: As of early 2026, 4.5 million people, including 2.9 million children, require urgent humanitarian assistance in Burkina Faso, according to UNICEF, driven by displacement, food insecurity and recurrent climate shocks. Across the wider central Sahel, an estimated 11.4 million people need critical food assistance, with 401,000 children suffering severe acute malnutrition, OCHA reported.
bf.why: Persistent food and nutrition gaps keep pressure on markets, aid budgets and rural livelihoods across the north and Sahel regions.

bf.headline: Security forces thwart 23rd coup plot against TraorÃƒÂ©, tied to exiled predecessor
bf.body: Security forces thwarted an attempted coup against transitional President Captain Ibrahim TraorÃƒÂ© in the early hours of January 3, 2026, marking what sources describe as the 23rd such plot since he took power in 2022. Intelligence reports say the plot was orchestrated from LomÃƒÂ©, Togo, where former leader Paul-Henri Sandaogo Damiba has lived in exile, and involved plans to assassinate key figures and seize institutions in Ouagadougou.
bf.why: Repeated coup attempts underline persistent instability at the top of government, a risk factor for investors and regional partners.

bf.headline: France and Burkina Faso sever diplomatic relations amid Sahel realignment
bf.body: France and Burkina Faso have severed diplomatic relations, according to The Africa Report, marking a further stage in the decline of Paris's influence across the Sahel. The move underscores the growing alignment of military-led governments in Burkina Faso, Mali and Niger with Russia, Turkiye and China.
bf.why: The rupture cuts a historic diplomatic channel and pushes trade, security and aid ties further toward new partners.

bf.headline: JNIM attacks kill at least 38 civilians in early 2026 as insurgency persists
bf.body: Three attacks in late January and early February 2026 by militants from Jama'at Nusrat al-Islam wal-Muslimin (JNIM) killed at least 38 civilians and saw nine women abducted, Human Rights Watch reported, as cited by Africa Defense Forum. The Global Terrorism Index has named Burkina Faso the country most affected by terrorism worldwide, with nine of the 20 deadliest global attacks in 2024 occurring there.
bf.why: Continued mass-casualty attacks keep large parts of the north off-limits to trade, farming and aid convoys.

bf.headline: Holders Ivory Coast eliminate Burkina Faso 3-0 at Africa Cup of Nations
bf.body: Defending champions Ivory Coast beat Burkina Faso 3-0 in the round of 16 at the Africa Cup of Nations, ending the Stallions' campaign and sending Ivory Coast into a quarterfinal meeting with Egypt, according to Al Jazeera.
bf.why: The early exit denies Burkina Faso a deep continental run that would have lifted national morale amid ongoing security strain.

bf.headline: Burkina Faso's gold output hits record as state deepens control of mining sector
bf.body: Burkina Faso's gold production has climbed to a record level as the government's nationalization drive accelerates, according to Africa News Desk, with five mines already transferred to state control and plans for ten new semi-mechanized, locally led mines scheduled for 2026. Gold makes up more than 70% of the country's export revenue, and the sector has drawn scrutiny after Burkina Faso nationalized the Boungou and Wahgnion mines for about $80 million, a fraction of their earlier $300 million valuation.
bf.why: Record output plus state control could boost government revenue but adds uncertainty for remaining foreign mining investors.

bi.headline: Ruling CNDD-FDD names President Ndayishimiye as 2027 presidential candidate
bi.body: Burundi's ruling CNDD-FDD party announced via social media that it has selected President Ãƒâ€°variste Ndayishimiye as its candidate for the 2027 presidential election, according to Burundi Times. The party, which has governed Burundi since 2005, gave few details beyond the announcement, but the move marks the formal start of positioning for the vote. Under Burundi's constitution, the president serves a seven-year term decided in a two-round system.
bi.why: Locks in the ruling party's succession plan more than a year before the vote, reducing near-term political uncertainty for investors and donors.

bi.headline: Ndayishimiye repeats accusation Rwanda backs RED-Tabara rebels near border
bi.body: President Ãƒâ€°variste Ndayishimiye said Rwanda "harbours malicious intentions toward Burundi," including alleged support for the RED-Tabara rebel group, in comments to Jeune Afrique reported by the International Crisis Group. He defended Burundi's troop deployment in DRC's South Kivu province, citing the presence of Rwandan forces and M23 rebels near Burundi's border as a security threat. Rwanda's foreign minister rejected the allegations.
bi.why: Continued border friction between Bujumbura and Kigali raises the risk of trade disruption and further military mobilization along an already tense frontier.

bi.headline: Seven opposition parties boycott Burundi's election-commission meeting
bi.body: Seven opposition parties, including the National Congress for Freedom, boycotted or walked out of a preparatory meeting held by Burundi's Independent National Electoral Commission (CENI) for the 2027 presidential election, according to the International Crisis Group. The parties denounced what they called CENI's refusal to acknowledge irregularities in the 2025 legislative elections.
bi.why: Early opposition distrust of the election body signals a contested run-up to 2027, a factor foreign observers and investors will watch for stability risk.

bi.headline: More than 71,000 Congolese refugees have crossed into Burundi since January
bi.body: The United Nations says more than 71,000 people fleeing violence in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo have crossed into Burundi since January, according to Al Jazeera. Arrivals have strained camps such as Musenyi in southeastern Burundi, where aid agencies have been distributing food and cooking oil from dwindling supplies.
bi.why: A sustained refugee influx adds pressure on food, aid budgets and public services in one of the world's poorest countries.

bi.headline: Burundi inflation eases to 11.4% in February, lowest reading since 2022
bi.body: Burundi's annual inflation rate fell to 11.4% in February 2026 from 12.6% in January, marking the lowest level since January 2022, according to Trading Economics data from the national statistics institute ISTEEBU. Food inflation stood at 27% year-on-year in February, down from 29.9% the prior month. Forecasters expect the headline rate to end the quarter near 14%.
bi.why: Slower price growth offers some relief to households after inflation topped 45% in April 2025, though food costs remain sharply elevated.

bi.headline: Burundi exports 1,235 tonnes of critical minerals in two-week period
bi.body: Burundi shipped 1,235 tonnes of critical minerals over a two-week span, Burundi Times reported, as the government pushes to expand the country's mining sector. Mining has been a key driver of growth alongside electricity generation and services, according to the African Development Bank.
bi.why: Mining exports are becoming a bigger cushion for foreign-currency earnings as Burundi grapples with persistent dollar shortages.

bi.headline: Burundi's widening exchange-rate gap fuels shortages, experts urge reform
bi.body: Burundi's widening gap between official and parallel exchange rates has distorted the economy for years, with experts calling for reforms to address shortages and rising prices, according to Breaking Burundi. The African Development Bank projects the current-account deficit will narrow to 6.3% of GDP in 2026 from prior levels, helped by gold and coffee exports, but warns the outlook remains vulnerable to fuel and foreign-currency constraints.
bi.why: The currency distortion is a key driver of fuel shortages and import costs that ripple through prices for everyday goods.

bi.headline: UN lists Burundi among 20 nations most vulnerable to climate change
bi.body: The United Nations ranks Burundi among the 20 countries most vulnerable to climate change, according to Al Jazeera. In 2024, heavy rains intensified by El NiÃƒÂ±o displaced nearly 100,000 people, though no official casualty figures have been released, and rising waters from Lake Tanganyika continue to affect displaced communities living in camps such as Gateri.
bi.why: Recurring flood displacement compounds an already stretched humanitarian response that is also absorbing refugees from DRC.

cm.headline: Biya postpones Cameroon's legislative and municipal polls, no new date set
cm.body: <cite index="9-3">President Paul Biya announced on Tuesday evening a "slight readjustment" of the timing of legislative and municipal elections that were expected at the start of February</cite>. <cite index="9-4,9-5">Originally scheduled for 2025, the elections had already been postponed once until early 2026, and no new date was set</cite>. <cite index="10-5">On 19 March 2026, the National Assembly voted to extend its mandate until 20 December 2026</cite>.
cm.why: Delayed legislative and local polls extend the ruling party's grip on parliament and postpone any real test of opposition strength after the disputed presidential vote.

cm.headline: Biya declared winner with 53.66% as rival calls result a 'masquerade'
cm.body: <cite index="14-1">Cameroon's President Paul Biya on 27 October 2025 was declared the winner of the country's presidential election, securing 53.66 percent of the vote, the Constitutional Council announced, results which his rival swiftly rejected</cite>. <cite index="14-4">Former government minister Issa Tchiroma Bakary came second with 35.2 percent</cite>. <cite index="14-5">Tchiroma denounced the announcement, telling AFP "there was no election; it was rather a masquerade"</cite>. <cite index="14-10">On 26 October 2025 four people were killed in clashes between security forces and supporters of the opposition in the economic capital Douala</cite>.
cm.why: The disputed result keeps political risk elevated for investors and residents in Douala and YaoundÃƒÂ© heading into a contested legislative cycle.

cm.headline: Cameroon growth seen slowing to 3.2% in 2026 as LNG vessel exits Kribi
cm.body: <cite index="25-2">The national economic committee forecasts growth of about 3.2% in 2026, down from 3.5% in 2025, before easing further to 3.1% in 2027</cite>. <cite index="25-6">The contract between Cameroon's National Hydrocarbons Corporation and Golar, which owns the floating LNG unit Hilli Episeyo, expires in July 2026</cite>. <cite index="25-12,25-13">During the first quarter, Cameroon's total exports fell 23.6% to CFA606.9 billion, with LNG exports dropping 28.4% and crude oil exports declining 14.4%</cite>.
cm.why: Weaker gas and oil export receipts squeeze the foreign-exchange pipeline the state relies on to service debt and fund imports.

cm.headline: Anglophone conflict nears decade mark with over 6,500 dead, UN says
cm.body: <cite index="36-1">The conflict between the government and separatists from the English-speaking minority, started in 2017, has killed over 6,500 people and has displaced 584,000 people, with an additional 73,000 refugees in Nigeria</cite>. <cite index="35-7">Separate attacks in December 2025 and January 2026 killed at least 23 people, most of them women and children, in Wowo and Gidado villages, north-west Cameroon</cite>. <cite index="34-9">On 19 March, the Supreme Court of Cameroon annulled the life sentences of ten separatist leaders known as the "Nera 10"</cite>.
cm.why: Ongoing violence and roadblocks in the Northwest and Southwest continue to disrupt trade routes, schooling, and cocoa and coffee farming in the affected regions.

sources.name: Global Centre for the Responsibility to Protect

cm.headline: Cimencam and Dangote Cement post combined 12.1% sales drop in Cameroon
cm.body: <cite index="5-1">Combined sales at Cimencam and Dangote Cement fell 12.1% in the first quarter</cite>. <cite index="5-1">Both companies also reported lower production during the period</cite>.
cm.why: Softer cement demand points to a slowdown in construction activity that feeds directly into jobs and housing costs.

cm.headline: Cameroon Development Corporation logs weakest banana export month of 2026
cm.body: <cite index="22-6">Cameroon Development Corporation (CDC), the country's only domestically owned banana exporter, recorded its weakest monthly export performance of 2026</cite>.
cm.why: A weak month for the state banana exporter dents rural employment and foreign-exchange earnings in the Southwest region.

cm.headline: Indomitable Lions top World Cup qualifying group after Cape Verde rout
cm.body: <cite index="42-1">Cameroon delivered a 4-1 victory over Cape Verde in their 2026 African World Cup qualifier at the Stade Omnisport RoumdÃƒÂ© Adjia</cite>. <cite index="42-3">The Indomitable Lions surged to the top of Group D with seven points, level with Libya but boasting a superior goal difference</cite>.
cm.why: A strong qualifying run keeps national attention and sponsorship interest on the squad ahead of decisive matches against Eswatini and Libya.

cm.headline: Indomitable Lionesses chase first WAFCON title in Morocco
cm.body: <cite index="46-2">Hosted in Morocco from July 26 to August 16, Cameroon's Lionnes Indomptables enter the tournament seeking to end decades without a continental women's title</cite>. <cite index="43-4">The team plays under newly appointed head coach Valentine Nguele and is inspired by emerging midfield star Naomi Eto, aiming also to reach the 2027 FIFA Women's World Cup</cite>.
cm.why: A deep run would boost domestic interest in women's football and sponsorship funding for the sport at home.

cf.headline: Bangui fuel shortage stretches into fourth week, driving black-market prices higher
cf.body: Queues at filling stations in Bangui have persisted for nearly a month, according to Radio Ndeke Luka, with drivers waiting hours as pumps run dry. In towns outside the capital, a litre of fuel is selling for 3,000 to 5,000 CFA francs, several times the official price, while authorities have offered no public explanation for the disruption. The National Assembly held a debate on the crisis as landlocked CAR remains dependent on fuel shipped through ports in Cameroon and the Republic of Congo.
cf.why: Prolonged fuel scarcity raises transport costs and threatens to slow trade and food distribution nationwide.

cf.headline: Gunmen kill Swiss national and soldier near Bangui in weekend attack
cf.body: A Swiss national and a Central African army soldier were killed on August 1 in an armed attack on the village of Imohoro, about 50 kilometers north of Bangui, according to Radio France Internationale. No group has claimed responsibility and the identity of the attackers remains unknown. The Central African armed forces have increased patrols and launched search operations in the area.
cf.why: An attack this close to the capital signals insecurity is spreading beyond the country's volatile rural periphery.

cf.headline: Armed groups kill around 10, wound UN peacekeepers in northeast border raid
cf.body: Armed groups attacked Am-Dafock sub-prefecture near the Sudanese border on June 30, killing roughly 10 people and injuring three UN peacekeepers, according to the International Crisis Group. The United Nations said the assailants included fighters affiliated with the Popular Front for the Renaissance of the Central African Republic and the Democratic Movement for the Rally of the Central African People.
cf.why: The raid underscores how instability along the Sudan border continues to threaten civilians and peacekeepers despite gains elsewhere.

cf.headline: UN Security Council extends CAR arms-group sanctions to July 2027
cf.body: The UN Security Council unanimously renewed sanctions targeting armed groups in the Central African Republic for one more year, according to Radio Ndeke Luka. Resolution 2827 also extends the mandate of the panel of experts monitoring enforcement, keeping the measures in place until July 31, 2027.
cf.why: Continued sanctions keep pressure on armed factions but signal the Council still views the security situation as unresolved.

cf.headline: Government troops and Wagner fighters briefly exchange fire in southeast town
cf.body: Government forces and Wagner Group elements clashed on June 24-25 in ZÃƒÂ©mio, Haut-Mbomou prefecture, leaving one woman dead and at least one soldier injured, according to the International Crisis Group. The clash was reportedly triggered by a disagreement over operational control in the town.
cf.why: Friction between state forces and their Russian-linked allies raises questions about command coordination in contested areas.

cf.headline: Heavy rains flood Bangui neighborhoods, damaging homes and markets
cf.body: Torrential rain on July 12 flooded the Miskine and Boy-Rabe districts in Bangui's 4th and 5th arrondissements, according to Radio Ndeke Luka. Several areas remained inundated afterward, with standing water reported in market aisles and damage to homes.
cf.why: Recurring urban flooding highlights gaps in Bangui's drainage infrastructure as the rainy season continues.

cf.headline: Health ministry battles growing cholera outbreak, watches for Ebola spillover
cf.body: The Central African Republic is contending with an expanding cholera epidemic, according to Radio Ndeke Luka. The health minister also called for vigilance against Ebola in Obo, near the border with the Democratic Republic of Congo, where an Ebola outbreak has spread to additional provinces.
cf.why: A dual disease threat near a porous border could strain the country's already limited health infrastructure.

cf.headline: Telecel completes first phase of 4G rollout in Bangui
cf.body: Telecel Centrafrique announced on July 14 the completion of the first phase of its 4G network deployment in the capital, according to Pravda RCA. Commercial director HervÃƒÂ© Pendeoro presented the milestone at a press briefing in Bangui.
cf.why: Expanded mobile broadband could support small business and financial services in a market with limited connectivity.

km.headline: Comoros suspends fuel price hikes after deadly Anjouan clashes
km.body: Comoros' government suspended new fuel prices on May 16, 2026, days after diesel and gasoline hikes of 46% and 35% respectively triggered nationwide strikes and deadly unrest. One person was killed and five injured in clashes between protesters and security forces in the Mpage area of Anjouan island, according to the local prosecutor's office. Energy Minister Aboubacar SaÃƒÂ¯d Anli said President Azali Assoumani chose to suspend the decrees to preserve peace, with the price increases originally tied to global oil costs linked to the Iran conflict.
km.why: Reverses a cost-of-living shock that had shut transport and shops nationwide, easing near-term pressure on households and fishing crews.

km.headline: At least 18 migrants drown off Comoros en route to Mayotte
km.body: At least 18 African refugees drowned after smugglers dropped them into the water off Comoros' Mitsamiouli coast in March 2026 while they tried to reach the French island of Mayotte, officials and rescuers said. About 30 others survived; many victims could not swim and had traveled from the Democratic Republic of Congo. The coastguard continued searching for four missing bodies, according to the interior minister.
km.why: Underscores the deadly toll of the Comoros-Mayotte migration route that keeps drawing thousands of Africans despite repeated tragedies.

km.headline: Police dismantle migrant-smuggling ring running Comoros-Mayotte crossings
km.body: French border police investigators broke up a large network organizing clandestine kwassa-kwassa boat crossings between the Comoros and Mayotte in a March 2026 operation. The organization dropped passengers on the islet of M'tsamboro before ferrying them onward, charging migrants multiple payments; investigators said the ring generated more than 210,000 euros in revenue.
km.why: Signals tighter law-enforcement pressure on the smuggling economy that fuels dangerous sea crossings from Comoros.

km.headline: Comoros economy set to grow 3.4% in 2025 on services, easing inflation
km.body: Comoros' GDP growth is projected at 3.4% in 2025, edging up from 3.3% in 2024, driven mainly by the services sector supported by commerce and easing inflation, according to the World Bank. Industry is expected to expand 3.3%, led by construction in transport, tourism and health, while agriculture, the largest employer of the poor, grows a modest 2.9%.
km.why: Modest growth signals limited fiscal room to cushion households from the fuel-price shocks now roiling the archipelago.

km.headline: More than 20,000 Comorians deported from Mayotte in 2025
km.body: French authorities deported more than 20,000 Comorians from Mayotte in 2025 amid tightened residence-permit rules and stepped-up security operations, according to InfoMigrants. Residents in Mayotte's KawÃƒÂ©ni slum described living in daily fear of expulsion as France pushes a law aimed at rebuilding the territory and restricting residency access.
km.why: A steady deportation pipeline keeps straining family ties and remittances between Comoros and its diaspora on Mayotte.

km.headline: Ruling CRC party keeps large parliamentary majority after 2025 vote
km.body: President Azali Assoumani's Convention for the Renewal of the Comoros won 28 of 33 seats in the first round of January 2025 legislative elections, according to results announced by the electoral commission, later confirmed near 31 seats by the Supreme Court after re-runs in contested constituencies. The president's son, Nour El Fath Azali, was elected with over 78% of votes in his constituency, while the main opposition party Juwa boycotted the poll citing a lack of transparency.
km.why: Cements one-party dominance in the assembly, limiting institutional checks as the government navigates the current fuel-price crisis.

km.headline: Comoros joins Africa Finance Corporation as 44th member state
km.body: Comoros became the 44th member of the Africa Finance Corporation on March 18, 2025, according to a Wikipedia timeline of the country's events. The move ties the small island economy more closely to a pan-African infrastructure and development financier.
km.why: Opens a potential new channel for infrastructure financing in a country with no domestic stock exchange or bond market.

km.headline: Azali outlines 'Vision 2026' economic plan in year-end address
km.body: President Azali Assoumani used a December 29, 2025 address from the Palais du Peuple in Moroni to lay out a long-term economic vision for the country, framing institutional stability as a precondition for development. The speech built on the earlier Plan Comores Ãƒâ€°mergence, for which Azali received the TrophÃƒÂ©e de l'AfricanitÃƒÂ© in 2022.
km.why: Sets the government's official growth narrative against which the May fuel-price backlash will be judged.

cg.headline: Sassou Nguesso wins fifth term with 94.8% in Congo-Brazzaville vote
cg.body: Republic of Congo's constitutional court confirmed President Denis Sassou Nguesso's re-election with 94.9% of the vote on a turnout of 65.9%, extending his rule to nearly 42 years. The March 15 election was boycotted by major opposition parties, with six lesser-known candidates on the ballot; one challenger's request to annul the vote was rejected by the court. The constitution bars Sassou Nguesso, 82, from running again when his new five-year term ends in 2031.
cg.why: A confirmed fifth term locks in policy continuity for investors and creditors negotiating with Brazzaville, but keeps political-risk premiums elevated.

cg.headline: Congo-Brazzaville seeks new IMF programme as debt tops 90% of GDP
cg.body: The Republic of Congo has formally asked to open negotiations with the IMF for a new economic and financial programme, according to Africanews, with public debt exceeding 90% of GDP. Budget revenue remains highly dependent on oil output and exposed to swings in global commodity prices. Brazzaville said the move follows a January CEMAC summit at which regional leaders agreed to align economic policy with an IMF framework to defend the CFA franc's peg; an IMF mission is expected in Brazzaville in the coming weeks.
cg.why: A fresh IMF deal would set the terms for future budget spending, debt relief and subsidy policy that directly affect fuel and food prices.

cg.headline: Congo-Brazzaville finance minister projects 5.3% growth for 2026
cg.body: Finance Minister Christian Yoka told the country's National Economic and Financial Committee that the economy is projected to grow 5.3% in 2026, driven by an oil-production rebound, rising liquefied-gas output and a 23% surge in private-sector credit, according to Brazzaville Insider. The banking sector's non-performing loan ratio fell to 13.5% from 16.5% in 2024, with provisioning coverage for bad loans rising to 65.1%. Independent verification of the government's figures remains limited given the country's statistical capacity.
cg.why: Faster growth and a healthier loan book point to more available credit for local businesses, though the forecast still hinges on volatile oil prices.

cg.headline: Cholera resurges on Brazzaville's Mbamou Island after nine-week lull
cg.body: A cholera outbreak that had gone quiet resurfaced in February 2026 on Mbamou Island and in Congo-Oubangui department, with 196 suspected cases and eight deaths recorded since mid-February, according to a UNICEF flash update. A third hotspot with 14 alerts and five deaths was later identified in Impfondo, near the Central African Republic border. Children under 15 account for roughly a third of suspected cases.
cg.why: Renewed cholera spread signals continuing gaps in clean water and sanitation access along the Congo River, a risk for river-trade and riverside communities.

cg.headline: Norwegian oil executives charged over $25 million in bribes to Congo president
cg.body: Two executives of Hemla Africa Holding, a subsidiary of Norwegian energy firm PetroNor E&P, were charged on January 26 with paying $25 million in bribes to President Denis Sassou Nguesso and his family, according to Wikipedia's chronicle of 2026 events in the Republic of the Congo, citing Africanews reporting. The case adds to scrutiny of foreign oil companies' dealings with Congolese officials.
cg.why: The case puts foreign-investor compliance risk in Congo's oil sector under an international spotlight, with potential knock-on effects for licensing and partnerships.

cg.headline: Congolese football federation chief convicted in absentia over FIFA funds
cg.body: Jean-Guy Blaise Mayolas, president of the FÃƒÂ©dÃƒÂ©ration Congolaise de Football, was convicted in absentia in Brazzaville on March 10 of embezzlement, money laundering and forgery tied to misused FIFA funds, receiving a life sentence along with family members. An Interpol arrest warrant was later sought, according to Wikipedia's 2026 timeline citing Guardian reporting.
cg.why: The verdict threatens the governance and international standing of Congolese football, a major source of national sporting pride.

cg.headline: Russian-backed consortium advances Pointe-Noire fuel pipeline plan
cg.body: The Republic of Congo approved a joint venture with Russian state-backed firms in June 2025 to build a petroleum-products pipeline between Pointe-Noire and Brazzaville under a build-own-operate-transfer deal, with Russia's ZNGS Prometey holding a 90% stake and Congo's national oil company SNPC the remaining 10%, according to industry tracker OG Analysis. Work on the project could begin in 2026, per Coface's country risk analysis, with construction expected to take about three years.
cg.why: The pipeline aims to ease chronic domestic fuel shortages by moving refined products inland, but ties Congo's energy infrastructure closely to Russian financing.

cg.headline: Congo, DR Congo advance Brazzaville-Kinshasa bridge tax accord
cg.body: Officials from the Republic of Congo and the Democratic Republic of Congo validated a bilateral agreement in February 2026 setting a harmonized tax and customs regime for the proposed Brazzaville-Kinshasa road-rail bridge over the Congo River, according to Wikipedia's project entry. The agreement is meant to allow the stalled request-for-proposals process for the roughly $550 million, 1,575-metre span to relaunch.
cg.why: A working tax framework removes a key hurdle to financing the bridge, which would be the first fixed link between the two capitals and a boost for cross-river trade.

ci.headline: Ivory Coast completes $3.5 billion IMF program, debt risk falls to low
ci.body: Ivory Coast completed its economic program with the International Monetary Fund and was reclassified as being at low risk of debt distress, becoming the only sub-Saharan African country with that status. The IMF Executive Board completed the sixth and final review of the country's Extended Credit Facility and Extended Fund Facility arrangements, as well as the fifth review of its Resilience and Sustainability Facility, making about $832.8 million available for immediate disbursement. Ivory Coast reduced its budget deficit to 3% of GDP in 2025, in line with the WAEMU ceiling, and public debt declined as a share of GDP for the first time in more than 10 years.
ci.why: A lower debt-risk rating should ease borrowing costs and reassure eurobond investors ahead of the government's 2026-2030 spending plans.

ci.headline: Ouattara's RHDP wins 197 of 255 seats in Ivorian legislative vote
ci.body: CÃƒÂ´te d'Ivoire's ruling Rally of HouphouÃƒÂ«tists for Democracy and Peace secured an absolute majority in the December 27, 2025 legislative elections. Provisional results announced by the Independent Electoral Commission showed the RHDP winning 197 seats across 155 constituencies, consolidating its dominance in the National Assembly, on turnout of 35.04 percent. The Democratic Party of CÃƒÂ´te d'Ivoire emerged as the main opposition force with 32 seats, while independent candidates captured 23 seats to become the third-largest bloc.
ci.why: A supermajority gives President Ouattara, 83, an unobstructed path to advance his economic agenda with little institutional check.

ci.headline: Ivory Coast cuts cocoa farmgate price 57% to 1,200 CFA francs/kg
ci.body: Ivorian authorities reduced the cocoa farmgate price by 57% to CFA 1,200 (about $2.13) per kilogram for the 2025/2026 mid-crop campaign. During the main season from October to February, authorities had fixed the price at CFA 2,800 per kilogram. Agriculture Minister Bruno KonÃƒÂ© said "this decision was not taken lightly," linking the cut to falling global cocoa prices.
ci.why: The sharp cut squeezes incomes for millions of smallholder farmers just as global cocoa prices retreat from last year's record highs.

ci.headline: Ghana, Ivory Coast align 2026/27 cocoa season to start September 1
ci.body: Ghana and CÃƒÂ´te d'Ivoire, the world's two biggest cocoa producers, will begin the 2026/27 cocoa season on September 1 and end it on August 31, 2027. The two governments aim to align fixed farm-gate prices in dollar terms to reduce smuggling and market distortions. Analysts cited by CNBC Africa said CÃƒÂ´te d'Ivoire's crop has performed better than expected, at around 2.2 million tons.
ci.why: Synchronized pricing and calendars could curb cross-border bean smuggling and strengthen both governments' leverage in global cocoa markets.

ci.headline: Eni sanctions Baleine Phase 3, to triple Ivorian oil output to 150,000 bpd
ci.body: Eni and its partners Petroci and Vitol approved the final investment decision for the Baleine Phase 3 project, the largest hydrocarbon discovery ever made in CÃƒÂ´te d'Ivoire. The full-field development will raise oil production from 60,000 to 150,000 barrels per day and gas output from 80 to 200 million cubic feet per day. All gas produced will go to the domestic market, expanding electricity generation and supporting industrial development, according to Eni.
ci.why: Tripled output would make oil and gas a far larger share of state revenue and could ease domestic power supply constraints.

ci.headline: Bridge Bank Group's Ivory Coast IPO oversubscribed within 24 hours
ci.body: Bridge Bank Group CÃƒÂ´te d'Ivoire, the lender backed by Senegalese billionaire YÃƒÂ©rim Sow, launched its initial public offering on the BRVM in Abidjan-Plateau. Subscription to its public share offering, launched July 20, 2026, was fully covered in less than 24 hours on the regional stock exchange serving the eight UEMOA member states.
ci.why: The rapid sellout signals strong regional investor demand for new BRVM listings after a broader market rally this year.

ci.headline: Ivory Coast's Elephants advance to World Cup knockout stage
ci.body: CÃƒÂ´te d'Ivoire's national football team advanced to the World Cup knockout stage following a win described by allAfrica as historic. A brace from winger Nicolas PÃƒÂ©pÃƒÂ© sent the Elephants through, according to a CAF report carried by allAfrica.
ci.why: A deep World Cup run would be one of the country's most unifying sporting moments in years, drawing nationwide attention.

ci.headline: Ivorian government dismisses coup rumors as false, says officials
ci.body: President Alassane Ouattara presided over a council of ministers meeting at the presidential palace in Abidjan after false rumors of a military coup spread rapidly across social media in CÃƒÂ´te d'Ivoire during the same period. Journalist Christelle KouamÃƒÂ© told The Cable, "there is no coup in CÃƒÂ´te d'Ivoire. The country is stable."
ci.why: The episode highlights how quickly unverified claims can spread online in a country still sensitive to past political crises.

eg.headline: Egypt's central bank holds rates at 19% as it lifts 2026 inflation forecast to 16-17%
eg.body: The Central Bank of Egypt kept its overnight deposit rate at 19% and lending rate at 20% for a second straight meeting, pausing its easing cycle. Policymakers cited recent inflation developments and global uncertainty, and raised their 2026 average inflation forecast to a 16%-17% range from an earlier 11% estimate, pointing to rising global energy prices and pound volatility against the dollar.
eg.why: Borrowing costs stay near multi-year highs, keeping loan and mortgage costs elevated for households and firms even as officials watch currency swings.

eg.headline: Egypt's non-oil PMI rises to 46.8 in July, seventh month of contraction
eg.body: S&P Global's Egypt Purchasing Managers' Index climbed to 46.8 in July from a 41-month low of 46.0 in June, though it stayed below the 50 line separating growth from contraction for a seventh consecutive month. New business intakes fell again on weak demand, high prices and shipping delays, prompting firms to cut output, staffing and purchases, even as early survey readings were consistent with annual GDP growth of about 4%.
eg.why: Private-sector activity is still shrinking even as headline growth holds up, a split that keeps hiring and new-order pipelines under pressure.

eg.headline: IMF raises Egypt's 2026 growth outlook to 4.6%
eg.body: The IMF's July 2026 World Economic Outlook update projects Egypt's economy will expand 4.6% in 2026, up from 4.4% in 2025, citing stronger-than-expected momentum in non-oil manufacturing, tourism and telecommunications. The upgrade marks a shift in the Fund's language from crisis stabilization toward a tentative expansion that still depends on external financing and further structural reform.
eg.why: A higher growth call supports Cairo's case for continued Gulf and multilateral financing, but analysts say the durability of the recovery is still unproven.

eg.headline: Rafah crossing keeps processing wounded Palestinians from Gaza
eg.body: Egyptian authorities said they were preparing to receive a fresh batch of wounded and sick Palestinians from Gaza for treatment through the Rafah crossing, part of an ongoing rotation of medical evacuations. Egypt's Health Ministry has set up a medical point at the crossing to examine arrivals, classify cases and transfer them to hospitals by ambulance.
eg.why: Egypt remains the main conduit for Gaza medical evacuations and aid, keeping Cairo central to the ceasefire's humanitarian track.

eg.headline: Egypt unveils Byzantine-era city and 18 more tombs in twin finds
eg.body: Egypt's Tourism and Antiquities Ministry announced a well-preserved fourth-century Byzantine-era residential city at Dakhla Oasis in the Western Desert, alongside 18 additional rock-cut tombs at the Marina el-Alamein site near Alexandria, bringing the tomb total there to 48. The Dakhla site includes houses, churches, administrative buildings and inscribed pottery detailing daily commercial life, while the Alexandria tombs yielded a granite sarcophagus and gold funerary artifacts.
eg.why: Officials are banking on high-profile antiquities finds to help drive tourist arrivals, a top source of foreign currency alongside Suez Canal fees.

eg.headline: Egypt's tourist arrivals hit record 19 million in 2025, up 21%
eg.body: Egypt drew a record 19 million tourists last year, a 21% increase from 2024, according to official figures, with arrivals in the first four months of 2026 running higher than the same period a year earlier. Tourism, alongside the Suez Canal, is a major source of foreign currency for the cash-strapped economy.
eg.why: A stronger tourism season translates directly into hard-currency inflows the central bank needs to defend the pound.

eg.headline: Cairo's heatwave breaks as temperatures ease 1-2Ã‚Â°C nationwide
eg.body: The Egyptian Meteorological Authority forecast a slight temperature drop of one to two degrees Celsius across northern Egypt, Greater Cairo and Upper Egypt, with satellite data indicating a break in the recent heatwave. Forecasters said conditions would gradually cool through the week.
eg.why: Lower temperatures ease strain on the power grid and reduce heat-related health risks after weeks of extreme heat.

eg.headline: Talaat Moustafa Group's H1 sales jump 59% to EGP 211 billion
eg.body: Egyptian real estate developer Talaat Moustafa Group reported first-half sales of EGP 211 billion (roughly $4.4 billion), a 59% increase, according to Daily News Egypt. The company is among the largest listed firms on the Egyptian Exchange by market value.
eg.why: Strong presales show real estate demand holding up despite high interest rates, a key driver of construction jobs and cement and steel demand.

gq.headline: Equatorial Guinea opens 24-block oil and gas licensing round to fight output slide
gq.body: Equatorial Guinea's Ministry of Hydrocarbons launched a new licensing round in April 2026, offering 24 exploration blocks, two onshore and the rest offshore, running until November. National crude production has fallen from 241,000 barrels a day at its 2010 peak to 55,000 barrels a day in 2023, according to OPEC data. Hydrocarbons still account for 42% of GDP, 95% of exports and 90% of public revenue, the African Development Bank estimates.
gq.why: New exploration acreage is the government's main lever to slow a 15-year revenue decline that funds most of the state budget.

gq.headline: IMF projects Equatorial Guinea growth of just 0.9% a year through 2030
gq.body: The International Monetary Fund expects Equatorial Guinea's oil- and gas-dependent economy to expand by an average of only 0.9% annually between 2025 and 2030 because of declining hydrocarbon production. The forecast underscores the country's struggle to diversify away from crude, which has powered the bulk of state revenue since the 1990s discoveries.
gq.why: Sub-1% growth leaves little room for new public spending as older oil fields keep depleting.

gq.headline: Chevron agrees terms on $690 million Aseng gas project with Equatorial Guinea
gq.body: Chevron's Noble Energy subsidiary has agreed terms with Equatorial Guinea on developing the Aseng gas project, moving the venture toward a final investment decision, according to Reuters. The project in the Douala Basin carries an initial investment of about $690 million and is meant to sustain liquefied natural gas supplies. Malabo is also reviving the $4.5 billion EG-27 gas project, backed by Afreximbank, which could produce 2.4 million tons of LNG a year over two decades.
gq.why: The deals represent rare fresh foreign investment as legacy oil operators such as ExxonMobil have exited the country.

gq.headline: Vice President TeodorÃƒÂ­n widens anti-corruption drive as succession looms
gq.body: Vice President TeodorÃƒÂ­n Obiang Mangue has launched an anti-corruption campaign targeting elites as the country faces what analysts call a tense leadership transition, according to the Bertelsmann Stiftung's BTI 2026 report. President Teodoro Obiang has publicly admitted massive mismanagement in government, an unusual acknowledgment that has fueled perceptions of instability within the ruling circle, the report said.
gq.why: Jockeying inside the ruling family ahead of a generational handover could shape how foreign investors and partners are treated.

gq.headline: Equatorial Guinea confirms capital shift from Malabo to Ciudad de la Paz
gq.body: Equatorial Guinea officially announced on 3 January that its capital will move from Malabo, on Bioko island, to the mainland city of Ciudad de la Paz. The government has cited strategic reasons for relocating administrative functions away from the island seat that has hosted the capital for decades.
gq.why: Shifting the seat of government to the mainland will redirect infrastructure spending, land deals and logistics contracts.

gq.headline: Cameroon, Equatorial Guinea sign deal to jointly develop Yoyo-Yolanda gas field
gq.body: Cameroon and Equatorial Guinea signed an agreement on 3 February to jointly extract natural gas from the cross-border Yoyo-Yolanda field. The pact adds to a series of gas partnerships Malabo has pursued as it tries to offset falling crude output with LNG production.
gq.why: A shared gas field with Cameroon could add a new production stream as Equatorial Guinea's own reserves mature.

gq.headline: Nzalang Nacional exit AFCON group stage after Algeria hand third straight loss
gq.body: Algeria beat Equatorial Guinea to finish Group E of the 2025 Africa Cup of Nations with a perfect record, eliminating the Nzalang Nacional after three consecutive defeats, according to Outlook India. The team had been drawn against Burkina Faso, Sudan and Algeria in the group phase.
gq.why: An early exit ends the host-region team's tournament run and closes out a difficult qualifying saga marked by an eligibility dispute over captain Emilio Nsue.

gq.headline: Pope Leo XIV's April visit to Malabo spotlights poverty despite oil wealth
gq.body: Pope Leo XIV arrived in Malabo on 21 April for the final leg of his four-nation Africa trip, the first papal visit to Equatorial Guinea since 1982, according to Vatican News. Despite the country's oil wealth, it ranks 133rd out of 193 nations on the UN's Human Development Index, with wealth distributed unevenly, the outlet reported.
gq.why: The visit drew global attention to the gap between Equatorial Guinea's hydrocarbon riches and living standards for most citizens.

er.headline: Ethiopia and Eritrea mass troops as Red Sea access dispute deepens
er.body: Ethiopian and Eritrean forces have built up along their shared border amid a dispute rooted in Addis Ababa's push for sea access, according to analysts tracking the standoff. The International Crisis Group says the risk of hostilities involving Ethiopia, Tigray and Eritrea remains high three years after the last major war in the area, and has urged outside powers to open back channels to defuse tensions. Ethiopia has accused Eritrea of backing armed factions inside Ethiopian territory, while relations have deteriorated since early 2025 over Eritrea's bid to regain access to the Assab port.
er.why: A slide toward renewed war would disrupt trade routes, displace civilians and draw in regional and Gulf powers.

er.headline: Isaias uses Independence Day speech to criticise US policy, sign Egypt maritime deal
er.body: President Isaias Afwerki used his 24 May Independence Day address marking Eritrea's 35th anniversary to question the policies of the Trump administration, particularly interventions in Iran and Venezuela, while cautioning against premature conclusions, according to the International Crisis Group. He went on to criticize decades of what he called reckless U.S. hegemony. Separately, Asmara and Cairo signed a maritime agreement.
er.why: The speech signals Asmara is hedging between wary engagement with Washington and closer ties with Cairo on Red Sea security.

er.headline: UK courts clear deportation of Eritrean asylum seekers to France under new pact
er.body: Britain's High Court and Court of Appeal have ruled against Eritrean asylum seekers contesting removal to France under the UK-France "one in, one out" migration scheme, with the first such deportation carried out after a man who fled Eritrea in 2019 over forced conscription lost his case. A second Eritrean man was removed days later after judges found the Home Office had sufficient grounds to reject his trafficking claim. Prime Minister Keir Starmer's government has called the removals proof the scheme works and says it plans to scale up returns.
er.why: The rulings set a legal precedent that is likely to accelerate returns of Eritrean Channel migrants to France.

er.headline: China's Zijin expands Bisha mine output with new pits as copper, zinc keep exports flowing
er.body: Zijin Mining says its Bisha copper-zinc operation in western Eritrea, the country's largest mining project, extracts 2.9 million tonnes of ore a year and in 2025 completed pre-stripping at the new Hambok open pit while starting production at the Asheli underground mine. Bisha has produced more than 1 million ounces of gold since output began, alongside 16,000-18,000 tonnes of copper and roughly 117,000 tonnes of zinc annually as of 2023, according to industry data. Mining accounts for over 90% of Eritrea's exports, leaving the economy exposed to global metals prices.
er.why: Continued expansion at Bisha underpins Eritrea's main source of foreign exchange and government revenue.

er.headline: Colluli potash project advances under Chinese ownership after Danakali exit
er.body: Control of the Colluli potash project, one of the world's largest sulphate-of-potash deposits with reserves estimated at 1.1 billion tonnes, has passed to China's Sichuan Road and Bridge Group after Australia's Danakali sold its 50% stake for $135 million plus a $31 million shareholder loan. The project, jointly held with Eritrea's state mining company ENAMCO, is designed to run for roughly 200 years and was projected to help lift Eritrea's GDP growth toward 3.3% by 2026 once production ramps up.
er.why: A running Colluli mine would diversify Eritrea's export base beyond gold and copper into fertiliser inputs for regional agriculture.

er.headline: Hundreds of Eritreans forcibly returned from Ethiopia face treason claims, UN says
er.body: Amnesty International reports that between December 2024 and 27 February 2025, more than 600 Eritreans who had sought refuge in Ethiopia were forcibly returned to Eritrea, where the government regarded their asylum claims as evidence of treason. The UN Special Rapporteur on Eritrea told the Human Rights Council that Asmara has taken no steps to reform its indefinite national service programme, a key driver of outward migration. Rights groups say the conscription policy continues to push large numbers of Eritreans to flee the country.
er.why: The returns policy raises safety risks for the region's largest refugee-producing population and pressures Ethiopia's asylum system.

er.headline: Girmay leads NSN's Tour de France bid as Eritrea's cycling profile grows
er.body: Eritrean sprinter Biniam Girmay heads an eight-rider NSN Cycling Team squad at the 2026 Tour de France, his first appearance for the team after signing a three-year contract that began this season. Girmay enters the race off his best early-season form since 2022, having taken a stage win and two top-10 finishes at the Baloise Belgium Tour, following his 2024 Tour campaign in which he won three stages and the green points jersey as the first African to claim any Tour classification.
er.why: Girmay's results keep Eritrea in global sports coverage and continue to draw young riders into the country's cycling programs.

er.headline: Eritrea's mining sector stays reliant on Chinese capital amid Western sanctions
er.body: Eritrea's international isolation continues to limit financial inflows into its mineral sector, with sanctions and human rights concerns having deterred Western investment and left China as the dominant player, according to bne IntelliNews. State-backed Chinese firms including Zijin Mining and Sichuan Road and Bridge now control the country's key gold, copper, zinc and potash projects. The country's gold reserves are estimated at 2 million ounces, with mining contributing about 20% of GDP in 2021.
er.why: Heavy reliance on Chinese capital shapes the terms of Eritrea's resource development and its limited access to diversified financing.

ke.headline: ODM presses for deputy president slot as Ruto's 2027 coalition talks intensify
ke.body: ODM Party Leader Oburu Oginga said on August 4 that he is qualified to be President William Ruto's running mate in 2027, arguing the deputy president post should be open for negotiation. His remarks follow ODM demands for a 50-50 split of government positions with the ruling UDA party, while Deputy President Kithure Kindiki has insisted his position is non-negotiable and that Mount Kenya will remain in government.
ke.why: The outcome of this coalition dispute will shape Ruto's 2027 ticket and regional political alliances, with knock-on effects for cabinet stability and policy continuity.

ke.headline: Kenya inflation rebounds to 6.5% as central bank sells KSh150bn infrastructure bond
ke.body: Kenya's inflation rate rebounded to 6.5%, according to a Standard Investment Bank weekly report, as the Central Bank of Kenya launched a KES 150 billion infrastructure bond offer. Liquidity conditions stayed stable, with the overnight interbank rate closing the week at an average of 8.75%.
ke.why: Faster price growth squeezes household budgets while the new bond sale will test investor appetite for government debt.

ke.headline: World Bank, IMF trim Kenya's 2026 growth forecast to below 5% on fuel costs
ke.body: The Central Bank of Kenya cut its 2026 growth forecast to 4.9% from 5.3%, while the IMF projected an even lower 4.5%, with higher fuel and energy costs linked to the Middle East conflict cited as the main driver. Transport costs alone climbed more than 16% over the year, directly hitting commuters and small traders.
ke.why: A softer growth outlook narrows the government's room to create jobs and manage debt ahead of the 2027 election cycle.

ke.headline: Nairobi bourse extends rally as Centum and Family Bank lead gainers
ke.body: The Nairobi Securities Exchange recorded a market capitalization of KES 4.05 trillion (about USD 31.2 billion) after a trading session that saw 29 gainers against 22 losers. Centum Investment Company led gainers with a 9.66% jump to KES 17.60 a share, followed by Family Bank at 9.38%, while Safaricom recorded the day's highest trading volume at 15.5 million shares.
ke.why: Broad-based gains signal renewed retail and institutional appetite for Kenyan equities after a prolonged market slump.

ke.headline: Health minister's handling of US Ebola facility draws court scrutiny
ke.body: A Kenyan court found that Health Cabinet Secretary Aden Duale disobeyed an order to halt construction at a proposed US-funded Ebola isolation facility for American nationals infected abroad, according to Al Jazeera. The facility at Laikipia Air Base had drawn weeks of protests amid fears it could expose Kenya to a disease it has never recorded, with a UN report finding some related facilities were staffed by trafficked foreign nationals.
ke.why: The dispute over the facility's legality keeps a politically sensitive US security partnership under judicial and public pressure.

ke.headline: Kenya marks second Gen Z protest anniversary under heavy security
ke.body: Kenya braced for renewed demonstrations on the second anniversary of the 2024 Gen Z-led protests, with President Ruto urging citizens not to demonstrate and calling for productivity instead. A commemoration marking the first anniversary the previous year turned violent when government forces killed more than 60 people, according to Al Jazeera.
ke.why: Recurring unrest around the protest anniversary remains a barometer of public frustration over living costs and police accountability that can disrupt business in central Nairobi.

ke.headline: Shilling holds near KSh129 per dollar, helping contain inflation
ke.body: The USD/KES exchange rate stood at 129.40 on August 4, down 0.04% from the previous session and roughly flat over the past year, according to Trading Economics. A stable shilling has kept the price of imported fuel and goods from rising even faster, though defending that stability limits the central bank's policy options.
ke.why: Currency stability is cushioning consumers and importers from the sharper price shocks otherwise being driven by global fuel costs.

ke.headline: Ruto unveils KSh3,000 monthly stipend for 106,000 village elders
ke.body: President William Ruto announced a KSh 3,000 monthly stipend and SHA health cover for 106,000 village elders, expanding their formal role within Kenya's local administration.
ke.why: The move widens a state-funded patronage network at the grassroots level ahead of the 2027 election cycle, adding to public spending commitments.

za.headline: Court halts Ramaphosa impeachment inquiry as EFF fights ruling in ConCourt
za.body: A South African court has paused the parliamentary committee investigating a possible impeachment case against President Cyril Ramaphosa tied to the Phala Phala farm scandal, according to eNCA. The Economic Freedom Fighters has since asked the Constitutional Court to reinstate the impeachment proceedings, arguing the committee must continue its work, while the impeachment committee met amid the ongoing legal battle.
za.why: The outcome will determine whether South Africa's head of state faces a formal impeachment process, a first-order political risk for markets and governance.

za.headline: SARB holds repo rate at 7% as inflation jumps to 5%, a two-year high
za.body: The South African Reserve Bank kept its benchmark repo rate unchanged at 7% on July 23, even after Statistics South Africa reported annual consumer inflation accelerated to 5% in June from 4.5% in May. The Monetary Policy Committee voted 4-2 to hold, with two members pushing for a 25-basis-point hike, and Governor Lesetja Kganyago said the bank is setting policy to return inflation to a 3% target over time.
za.why: Borrowing costs stay put for now, but a hotter inflation print keeps pressure on the rand and on households' loan repayments.

za.headline: Eskom marks 441 days without load shedding, its best run since 2018
za.body: South Africa has gone 441 consecutive days without power cuts since 16 May 2025, Eskom said, with electricity demand met 100% of the time between April and July. Unplanned outages on 26 July fell to 4,562MW, the lowest since June 2018, and diesel spending dropped 84% year-on-year to R746.41 million, while six of nine provinces have been fully removed from load reduction schedules.
za.why: A stable grid removes one of the biggest drags on business investment and household costs, though rising Eskom tariffs still squeeze budgets.

za.headline: ANC opens talks to expand 10-party GNU coalition after budget rifts
za.body: The African National Congress will hold discussions over two to three weeks on expanding its coalition government following disputes with the Democratic Alliance over the budget, secretary-general Fikile Mbalula said. The GNU currently controls more than 70% of parliamentary seats through the ANC, DA, Inkatha Freedom Party and seven smaller parties, and any new entrant requires approval from existing members under the coalition's founding agreement.
za.why: A wider or reshuffled coalition would reset the balance of power ahead of local elections and shape how far pro-market reforms can go.

za.headline: Rand hovers near R16.40/dollar as manufacturing PMI weakens further
za.body: The rand traded around 16.40 to the US dollar in early August, extending a recovery from a more than three-month low of 16.98 hit on 24 July, as global risk sentiment improved. Domestically, PMI data showed South Africa's manufacturing sector weakened further in July on soft export demand, even as the currency is still up 8.41% over the past 12 months.
za.why: A firmer rand eases import costs, but soft factory output signals the real economy is lagging the currency's gains.

za.headline: Gold miners lead JSE gains as bullion rally lifts Gold Fields' market cap
za.body: Gold Fields (GFI) has seen its market capitalisation climb to roughly R824.3 billion with a one-year share return of 164.1%, according to Simply Wall St data, as gold's bull run continues to support gold-sensitive assets including the rand. Barclays has said the ongoing gold rally provides a fundamental lift to gold-linked emerging-market currencies and miners alike.
za.why: Gold's rally is cushioning the JSE and the rand even as broader manufacturing and consumer data soften.

za.headline: Gauteng legislature speaker under scrutiny over R6m Venezuela trip
za.body: The Gauteng provincial legislature speaker and staff spent about R6 million on a trip to Venezuela, drawing criticism after it emerged the visit came days after US military action, according to reports carried on Google News South Africa. The spending has added to public scrutiny of provincial government travel costs amid tight budgets.
za.why: The episode fuels debate over public spending oversight as provinces face fiscal constraints.

za.headline: Electricity tariff hikes of up to 9% squeeze households despite stable grid
